issues.failure_explanation: The residual $R_\theta(D_k)=\int_{\partial D_k}(U_\theta n_t + F(U_\theta)\cdot n_x)dS$ involves only the network's own state and flux; no prescribed boundary datum enters the loss. Two networks with different (wrong) boundary traces but internally balanced fluxes yield identical residuals on boundary-touching volumes, so evaluating $R_\theta(D_k)$ cannot enforce, e.g., a prescribed inflow state. The claimed enforcement mechanism does not exist in the defined loss, and no experiment prescribes boundary data.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's central step is false. (i) $\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}$ is built from the Kružkov pair $(|U_\theta-k|, \text{sgn}(U_\theta-k)(F(U_\theta)-F(k)))$, whereas $L_{\mathrm{ent}}$ penalizes boundary integrals of the physical pair $(\eta,q)$ one-sidedly; these are different residuals, so 'corresponding exactly' is wrong. (ii) Integrating $\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}$ by parts over a cell yields $\varphi$-weighted boundary terms plus an interior term $-\int_{D_i}\varphi(\partial_t|U_\theta-k|+\nabla\cdot q_k(U_\theta))$, i.e. the strong residual of $U_\theta$, which the boundary-flux losses do not control; for smooth $U_\theta$ the unweighted cell-boundary terms cancel in the sum over a partition, so $\sum_i|R_{\mathrm{cons}}(D_i)|$ cannot bound the residual (e.g. oscillatory interior residuals with vanishing cell means are invisible to the losses but contribute to $E_R$). (iii) The losses are means $(1/N_D)\sum$ over dynamically sampled overlapping volumes, not a partition, so $\sum_i|D_i|\neq|\Omega\times(0,T)|$, and the Cauchy–Schwarz step produces a factor $\sqrt{N_D}$ that the stated bound omits; the one-sided loss also bounds only $E_\theta^+$, not $|R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i,k)|$. (iv) The statement is false as written: for $U_\theta=u$ the exact entropy solution of the Burgers Riemann shock problem, $R_\theta\equiv0$ and $E_\theta\le0$ on every control volume, hence $L_{\mathrm{cons}}=L_{\mathrm{ent}}=0$, while $E_R(u)$ equals the positive entropy dissipation at the shock, so the claimed bound reads $E_R(u)\le 0$.

failure_location.quote: Applying the divergence theorem on each $D_i$, the continuous residual translates into boundary flux integrals, corresponding exactly to the local conservation residual $R_{\mathrm{cons}}(D_i)$ and entropy residual $R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i, k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must redefine the losses as two-sided Kružkov-type residual controls over a genuine partition with a consistent normalization (sums, not means) and prove a new cell-level estimate bounding the interior strong residual contribution to $E_R$ — i.e. new proof architecture for the whole convergence section, or abandonment of the stated rate.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's only link between the trained losses and the dual-norm truncation error fails; Step 3 of Theorem thm:added-2 collapses with it, so the advertised explicit $L^1$ convergence rate and the abstract/introduction/conclusion claims of a 'rigorous convergence analysis' and a 'first explicit $L^1$ convergence rate' are unsupported.
issues.title: Lemma 1's reduction of the Kruzhkov residual to the control-volume losses is invalid
issues.why_classification: The stated inequality is false even for the exact entropy solution, and the losses as defined are structurally incapable of bounding $E_R$; every supported resolution requires a new construction and a different, weaker theorem, so the paper's central theoretical result does not survive in comparable form.

issues.failure_explanation: With $E_R(v)=\sup_{k,\varphi}\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}(v)$ taken over signed residuals with $\varphi\ge0$, the stated estimate is false. Counterexample: Burgers with $u_0=\mathbf{1}_{x>0}$ and $v$ the self-similar expansion shock ($v=0$ for $x<t/2$, $v=1$ for $x>t/2$). Then $v$ is a weak solution, bounded, with $TV(v(\cdot,t))=1$, so it satisfies the theorem's only hypotheses. For every $k\notin(0,1)$ the residual vanishes identically ($|v-k|$ is affine on the jump states), and for $k\in(0,1)$ it equals $-(1/4)\int_0^T\varphi(t/2,t)dt\le0$; since $\varphi\equiv0\in\mathcal{A}$, $E_R(v)=0$. The bound then gives $\|v(T)-u(T)\|_{L^1}\le0$, but the exact solution is a rarefaction and the $L^1$ error is positive (equal to $1/8+1/8=1/4$ on $(-1,1)$ at $T=1$). The cited Bouchut–Perthame estimate requires a two-sided (absolute-value) residual, which the paper's definition of $E_R$ does not provide.

failure_location.quote: \|v(\cdot, T) - u(\cdot, T)\|_{L^1(\Omega)} \leq \|v(\cdot, 0) - u_0\|_{L^1(\Omega)} + C \sqrt{TV(u_0) \cdot \sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(v(\cdot, t)) \cdot \sqrt{E_R(v)}},

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine $E_R$ as the two-sided quantity of Bouchut–Perthame, e.g. $\sup_{k,\varphi}|\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}(v)|$ (or allow sign-changing admissible test functions); the stated estimate then coincides with the cited theorem. A contained definitional repair.
issues.overall_effect: The $L^1$ error estimate underlying the entire convergence analysis is false as stated: approximate solutions that violate entropy (the very case the entropy loss is meant to exclude) are assigned $E_R=0$, so Theorem thm:added-2, which applies this estimate with $v=U_\theta$, loses its foundation independently of Lemma lem:added-1.
issues.title: Stated Bouchut–Perthame estimate is false for the one-sided residual (expansion shocks undetected)
issues.why_classification: A local, standard correction of the residual's definition restores a true estimate of the same strength for this theorem itself; no new proof architecture is needed for thm:added-1 as stated.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 2 asserts that the TVD regularization 'ensures' a uniform bound $\sup_t TV(U_\theta)\le M$, but $L_{\mathrm{TVD}}$ is only a soft penalty inside the training objective (weight 1, competing with $L_{\mathrm{cons}}$ and $L_{\mathrm{ent}}$) and is even evaluated by a stochastic sampling rule that does not compute the supremum; no mechanism or argument in the source enforces any $\theta$-uniform $M$. For each fixed $\theta$ such an $M(\theta)$ exists trivially, but then $K_{\mathrm{opt}}=C\sqrt{TV(u_0)M(\theta)}\,|\Omega\times(0,T)|^{1/4}$ depends on $\theta$, contradicting the stated independence, and the convergence conclusion (losses $\to0$ $\Rightarrow$ $L^1$ convergence) fails, since along a minimizing sequence the TV bounds may grow without any controlling mechanism.

issues.failure_explanation: The hard temporal ansatz $U_\theta=(1-\tau)U_0+\tau\mathcal{N}_\theta$ with $\tau(0)=0$ forces $U_\theta(\cdot,0)=u_0$ exactly, so every WE-PINNs relative error at $t=0.0$ must be identically zero; Step 1 of Theorem thm:added-2 relies on precisely this. Yet every table reports nonzero WE-PINNs errors at $t=0.0$ (e.g. $E_{L^1}=8.07\times10^{-3}$ and $E_{L^\infty}=7.95\times10^{-1}$ for the Burgers Riemann problem; $E_{L^1}=1.776\times10^{-3}$ for the dam-break depth). Hence the reported runs cannot implement the construction on which the theory relies: either the ansatz was not used, or the tabulated quantities are not the defined errors. The paper's theoretical setting and its own experimental evidence are mutually inconsistent.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all cases, the entropy functions are convex and the corresponding entropy fluxes satisfy the compatibility condition with the physical flux, ensuring consistency with the entropy inequality.

issues.failure_explanation:
For the 1D shallow-water system with $U=(h,m)$, $\eta=m^2/(2h)+gh^2/2$ (convex), compatibility $
abla_U q=
abla_U\eta\,
abla_U F$ forces $q=u(\eta+	frac12 gh^2)=	frac12 hu^3+gh^2u$ (the physical energy flux $u(E+p)$). The stated $q=\eta u=	frac12 hu^3+	frac12 gh^2u$ has gradient $(gm/2-m^3/h^3,\; gm/2+3m^2/(2h^2))$, which differs from the required $(gm-m^3/h^3,\; gh+3m^2/(2h^2))$ in both components. Hence $(\eta,q)$ as given is not an entropy pair for the shallow-water equations, the appendix's blanket compatibility claim is false (the Burgers and Euler pairs given are correct), and the entropy loss $L_{\mathrm{ent}}$ used for the shallow-water experiments penalizes an inequality that is not the entropy condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the shallow-water flux by the compatible one $q=u(\eta+\tfrac12 gh^2)$ (componentwise $u(E+p)$ in 2D) and re-validate the shallow-water experiments, whose entropy enforcement was performed with the wrong pair.
issues.overall_effect: The entropy-admissibility mechanism is mis-specified for the shallow water experiments: the residual $E_\theta$ and the loss $L_{\mathrm{ent}}$ penalize a quantity that is not an entropy inequality, so the claimed integral-form entropy admissibility for the SWE tests (and the appendix's consistency guarantee) fails for that model.
issues.title: Shallow-water entropy flux stated in Appendix C is not compatible with the physical flux
issues.why_classification: The fix of the pair is one line, but the SWE experiments' admissibility mechanism and their interpretation depend on the wrong pair, so a contained re-validation is required; the method and the other two models are unaffected.
